0.0.n: Used to introduce the closing remarks rather than answer a question.

0.2.n: With の, it specifies the current video.

0.3.n: Links 今回 to 動画, identifying which video.

0.4.n: The topic of the question; a topic particle is omitted in speech.

0.6.n: The お prefix makes 楽しみ respectful in this expression addressing viewers.

0.7.n: いただけました is the polite past of いただける; でしょう adds extra softness to this respectful question.

0.8.n: Ends the sentence as a polite question.

1.0.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

1.2.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

1.4.n: Part of the English channel name The Game Gallery.

1.6.n: A borrowed English word following the channel's name.

1.7.n: Marks the channel as what the speaker is discussing.

1.8.n: Here です helps create a polite pause before the main statement.

1.9.n: Softens the pause and keeps the listener engaged.

1.11.n: Needs な before the noun it describes.

1.12.n: Connects さまざま to ボードゲーム so it can describe the games.

1.13.n: Japanese does not require a plural ending here.

1.14.n: Follows the subject matter and describes the noun 話題 that comes next.

1.15.n: Refers to the board-game subjects the channel covers.

1.16.n: Marks 話題 as what the channel delivers.

1.17.n: The お prefix forms part of the humble expression お届けする, used for bringing content to viewers.

1.18.n: しております is a humble, polite version of しています, describing the channel's ongoing activity.

2.0.n: The name of the video platform.

2.1.n: Connects YouTube to 方 in a roundabout way of introducing the platform.

2.2.n: In YouTubeの方, 方 loosely indicates the platform, rather than a physical direction.

2.3.n: Marks YouTubeの方 as the topic.

2.4.n: Part of ですね, used here to pause politely before continuing.

2.5.n: Adds a conversational, listener-friendly tone to the pause.

2.7.n: Combines with 登録 to refer to subscribing to a channel.

2.8.n: With チャンネル, 登録 means subscribing rather than registering an account.

2.9.n: Connects チャンネル登録 to the softening filler 方.

2.10.n: A roundabout filler after チャンネル登録; it adds no essential information.

2.11.n: Marks チャンネル登録の方 as the action requested with する.

2.12.n: して is the linking form of する; いただきます humbly frames the viewer's action as a favor.

2.13.n: Introduces the expected result of subscribing, which follows in the next line.

3.0.n: The speaker refers to himself with this neutral, polite pronoun.

3.1.n: Marks 私 as the person uploading the video.

3.2.n: Refers to a video the speaker adds to the platform.

3.3.n: Connects 動画 to 方 in a roundabout spoken expression.

3.4.n: A filler after 動画; it does not indicate a direction here.

3.5.n: Marks 動画の方 as what the speaker uploads.

3.6.n: Polite past form of 登録する, literally registering something, used here for adding a video.

3.7.n: Follows the verb phrase to mean the time when that action happens.

3.8.n: Marks 時 as the point when the notification can happen.

3.10.n: Refers back to the new video or the fact that it has been uploaded.

3.11.n: Marks それ as the information that can be communicated.

3.12.n: Creates a polite pause within the unfinished sentence rather than ending a statement.

3.13.n: Keeps the listener engaged during the speaker's pause.

3.15.n: 素早い changes its final い to く to describe how information is conveyed.

3.16.n: The お prefix makes 伝え part of a respectful expression for informing viewers.

3.17.n: Follows お伝え to express the ability to inform viewers.

3.18.n: With に and なる, describes reaching a state where something is possible.

3.19.n: Links よう to なっております, indicating the resulting arrangement.

3.20.n: A humble, polite version of なっています, describing an arrangement already in place.

3.21.n: Gives the reason for the subscription request that follows.

4.0.n: Adds warm encouragement to the request.

4.1.n: Combines with 登録 to name the action the speaker wants viewers to take.

4.2.n: チャンネル登録 is the standard expression for subscribing to a channel.

4.3.n: Connects チャンネル登録 to the roundabout filler 方.

4.4.n: Softens the phrasing without adding essential meaning; the object particle を is omitted after it.

4.6.n: Combines with いたします to make a courteous request of viewers.

4.7.n: The polite form of いたす, a humble alternative to する, makes the request more formal.

0.lit: Well, this time's video, were you able to enjoy it, I wonder?
0.tip: お楽しみいただけましたでしょうか is a very polite way to ask whether viewers enjoyed something.

1.lit: As for The Game Gallery channel, you see, we are delivering topics concerning various board games.
1.tip: しております is a humble, polite alternative to しています, often used when presenting a service.

2.lit: As for the YouTube side, you see, if you kindly do channel subscription,
2.tip: と after a polite verb introduces an expected result: if you subscribe, something will happen.

3.lit: When I have registered a video, that, you see, is arranged so we can convey it quickly, so,
3.tip: できるようになっております means things are arranged so that something can be done.

4.lit: By all means, channel subscription, we humbly request.
4.tip: お願いいたします is a more formal, humble version of お願いします.
